quests.title: Penny Path Compass Shop Counter Quest
quests.visitSkill: Turning a small object choice into a clear story problem
quests.visitFit: Adult-led visit table quest for a grandparent, relative, neighbor helper, library family table, or homeschool co-op pair who want a short shared writing start.
quests.adultSetup: Print one page, place a coin-sized token or paper circle beside the pencil, and invite the writer to invent a shop helper without using real family details.
quests.kidDirection: Choose the pretend compass shop object, decide what it points toward, and write a tiny story problem that stays friendly and make-believe.
quests.hostPrompt: Offer two optional choices: a compass that points to a misplaced button or a compass that points to a quiet shelf; let the writer choose or invent a third option.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The compass shop counter holds ____________________.
The penny path points toward ____________________.
The shop helper notices one odd detail: ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: The helper can follow the tiny arrow to ____________________.
The helper can ask the shelf keeper about ____________________.
The choice I want in my story is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: First, the compass spins when ____________________.
Next, the helper discovers ____________________.
The story problem is solved by ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: One idea I liked from our visit talk was ____________________.
One object I can add to the shop scene is ____________________.
My story can continue when ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: circle the compass direction and write one shelf clue: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Start another penny path scene with a pretend object that points to ____________________.

quests.title: Tidepool Timekeepers Lab Minute Jar Quest
quests.visitSkill: Using sequence words to build a calm science-fantasy scene
quests.visitFit: Adult-led visit table quest for mixed-age family visits, library tables, and homeschool co-op days where the adult helps order three gentle events.
quests.adultSetup: Print the quest, set out a pencil, and invite the writer to imagine a harmless lab tool such as a shell marker, pebble dial, or minute jar.
quests.kidDirection: Pick the lab tool, decide what changes first and next, and draft a short tidepool scene with clear order words.
quests.hostPrompt: Offer optional talk choices: What does the lab tool show, what changes beside it, and what should the timekeeper do next?

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The tidepool timekeeper opens a minute jar labeled ____________________.
Inside the jar, the tiny clue looks like ____________________.
The lab table changes when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: First, the timekeeper should check ____________________.
Next, the lab helper should compare ____________________.
Last, the scene should pause near ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: At the start, the minute jar shows ____________________.
After that, the tidepool clock makes ____________________.
The timekeeper writes a note about ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: One sequence word I used today was ____________________.
One lab detail from our talk was ____________________.
The next gentle experiment could be ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: number three lab clues and finish this line: clue one is ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Continue the timekeeper story when the minute jar opens near ____________________.

quests.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Kind Repair Quest
quests.visitSkill: Writing a character action that shows helpfulness
quests.visitFit: Adult-led printable visit quest for a relaxed table where an adult and writer invent a garden helper, a small machine, and a cooperative fix.
quests.adultSetup: Print the page, place a pencil near any ordinary table object, and invite the writer to pretend the object is a gentle garden gear.
quests.kidDirection: Invent a greenhouse helper, choose what the gear should help, and write one action that shows the helper being thoughtful.
quests.hostPrompt: Offer optional choices: the gear can lift a tiny shade, turn a seed tray, or ring a soft bell for the next helper.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The greenhouse helper carries ____________________.
The garden gear is shaped like ____________________.
The plant table needs help with ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: The helper can adjust the gear beside ____________________.
The helper can trade tools with ____________________.
The most helpful choice is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: The gear clicks softly when ____________________.
The helper shows care by ____________________.
The garden changes in a good way because ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: One helpful action from my story is ____________________.
One greenhouse sound I want to keep is ____________________.
The next page could begin beside ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: sketch or list the garden gear, then write its job here: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Add a new greenhouse helper who brings the tool ____________________.

quests.title: Pantry Measurement Mystery Spoon Trail Quest
quests.visitSkill: Adding exact details and cause words to a mystery scene
quests.visitFit: Adult-led visit table quest for a grandparent, relative, neighbor helper, library table, or co-op adult who wants a cozy object-based writing prompt.
quests.adultSetup: Print the page, point to one safe ordinary object on the table, and remind the writer that all pantry clues are pretend.
quests.kidDirection: Choose three invented pantry clues, add one exact amount, and explain what the helper thinks happened.
quests.hostPrompt: Offer optional choices: a spoon trail, a flour dot map, or a measuring cup clue; invite the writer to pick the calmest mystery.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The pantry helper finds a spoon trail beside ____________________.
The first pretend clue measures ____________________.
The mystery shelf looks different because ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: The helper should compare ____________________.
The clue could mean ____________________.
The cause word I want to use is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: The measuring cup tips toward ____________________.
The pantry mystery becomes clearer when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: One exact detail I added was ____________________.
One pretend clue from our talk was ____________________.
The next mystery note could explain ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: write the three pantry clues as a list: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Continue the spoon trail mystery with a new pretend clue near ____________________.
